title.en: Reference models: OSI, TCP/IP and the five layers we use
title.zh: 参考模型：OSI、TCP/IP 与我们用的五层

description.en: Understand why a layering blueprint that everyone recognises must come first, what OSI's seven layers and TCP/IP's four layers each do, why OSI lost, and how this course's five layers carry an HTTPS request onto the wire.
description.zh: 弄清为什么要先有一张大家都认的分层蓝图，OSI 七层和 TCP/IP 四层各管什么，OSI 为什么输了，以及本课程的五层怎样把一次 HTTPS 请求带到线上。

name.zh: 本课程使用的五层混合模型 (hybrid reference model)

name.en: Origins of the Internet: the telephone system, Baran, ARPANET
name.zh: 互联网的起源 (origins of the Internet: telephone system, Baran, ARPANET)
分层、协议与封装 (layers, protocols, encapsulation)

description.en: Thinking today's Internet runs OSI's seven-layer protocols; in fact it runs TCP/IP, and OSI survives mainly as a model.
description.zh: 以为今天的互联网跑的是 OSI 的七层协议；其实跑的是 TCP/IP，OSI 主要作为模型留了下来。

description.en: Confusing the “Internet layer” in the TCP/IP model with the global Internet (the Internet).
description.zh: 把 TCP/IP 模型里的『Internet 层』和全球的互联网 (the Internet) 混为一谈。

description.en: Thinking the seven layers and four layers map one to one, or thinking that because the presentation and session layers “do not exist” their functions are done by nobody.
description.zh: 以为七层和四层是一一对应，或者以为表示层、会话层『不存在』就是它们的功能没有人做。

description.en: Thinking a router opens the packet up to the application layer; in fact a router implements only the lower three layers.
description.zh: 以为路由器会拆开到应用层；其实路由器只实现下三层。

description.en: Treating a reference model as the protocol itself: OSI's model survived, but OSI's protocols never became popular.
description.zh: 把参考模型当成协议本身：OSI 的模型留下了，OSI 的协议没有流行。

description.en: Treating Host-to-network and Link as two different layers; they are two names for the same bottom layer of TCP/IP.
description.zh: 把 Host-to-network 和 Link 当成两个不同的层；它们是 TCP/IP 最下面同一层的两个名字。

chapter.en: Why agree on a standard first

title.en: What happens without a standard

prompt.en: Suppose every company designs its own network: company A makes network cards, company B makes routers, company C writes website software, and they have never talked to each other. If you plug A's network card into B's router, will it work?
prompt.zh: 假设每家公司都自己设计网络：A 公司造网卡，B 公司造路由器，C 公司写网站软件，彼此从没商量过。把 A 的网卡接上 B 的路由器，能通吗？

label.en: Yes, network cable sockets are all standard
label.zh: 能通，网线的口子都是通用的

feedback.en: A plug that fits only shows the connector is suitable. How a packet is laid out, how addresses are written, how many bits are sent per second: none of this has been agreed yet.
feedback.zh: 口子插得进去只说明插头合适。分组怎样排版、地址怎么写、一秒发多少比特，都还没有约定。

label.en: Most likely not: each has its own conventions for packet format, addresses and speed
label.zh: 多半不通：分组格式、地址、速率各家各有各的约定

label.en: Yes, just a bit slower
label.zh: 能通，只是会慢一点

feedback.en: The problem is not slowness but failing to understand each other: what one side sends, the other cannot read at all.
feedback.zh: 问题不是慢，而是对不上话：一方发的东西，另一方根本读不懂。

explain.en: For two sides who have never talked to each other to understand each other, there must be an agreement everyone recognises. The skeleton of that agreement is the reference model.
explain.zh: 要让从没商量过的两方也能对上话，得有一份大家都认的约定。这份约定的骨架，就是参考模型。

title.en: Reference model: a blueprint everyone recognises
title.zh: 参考模型：大家都认的一张蓝图

text.en: A **reference model** is an abstract description of a set of **concepts and the relations between them**. In networks it answers only a few things: how many layers, what each layer does, and how layers deal with each other and how two hosts deal with each other. Which protocols or wires to use, it does not care.
text.zh: **参考模型** (reference model) 是对一组**概念以及它们之间关系**的抽象描述。放到网络里，它只回答几件事：分几层，每层管什么，层与层之间、两台主机之间怎样打交道。具体用什么协议、什么线，它不管。

text.en: The unlabelled block diagram on slide 3 is what is left of lesson 1's layering figure once the names are removed: a stack of layers, with horizontal conversation between the same layers (dashed lines) and vertical handover between layers (solid lines). The names and protocols are filled in by specific models and implementations.
text.zh: 课件第 3 页那张没写字的框图，就是第 1 课的分层图拿掉名字之后剩下的骨架：一摞层，同层之间横向对话（虚线），层与层之间纵向交接（实线）。名字和协议，由具体的模型和实现去填。

text.en: Why is such a diagram needed first? The slides give three reasons. Each one matches a problem that would arise without it.
text.zh: 为什么要先有这样一张图？课件给了三条理由。每一条，都对应一个没有它就会出的问题。

rows.en: Networks are complex, and a model can **simplify the design**
rows.zh: 网络很复杂，模型能**简化设计**

rows.en: One team has to think about wires, addresses, retransmission and web pages all at once; change one thing and everything is thrown into disorder
rows.zh: 一个团队要同时想线、地址、重传、网页……改一处，全盘都乱

rows.en: Split into layers first, and design and change each layer on its own
rows.zh: 先按层拆开，每层单独设计、单独改

rows.en: It gives different organisations a **common baseline**
rows.zh: 给不同组织一个**共同的基准**

rows.en: Company A's network card, company B's router and company C's software each follow their own format, and none can connect to another
rows.zh: A 公司的网卡、B 公司的路由器、C 公司的软件，各按各的格式，谁也接不上谁

rows.en: Everyone develops against the same blueprint, each making one piece, and the pieces still fit together
rows.zh: 大家按同一张蓝图开发，各做一块，也能拼在一起

rows.en: **An abstract model, with matching implementations to validate it**
rows.zh: **抽象的模型，加对应的实现来验证**

rows.en: With only a blueprint, nobody knows it can really be built and run; with only implementations, nobody can explain why they are the way they are
rows.zh: 只有蓝图，没人知道它真做得出来、跑得动；只有实现，又讲不清它为什么这样

rows.en: The model explains the idea, and the implementation tests it
rows.zh: 模型说清思路，实现检验它

text.en: The third reason deserves some thought. A model is on paper, and what makes sense on paper may be slow when built, or may clash. So good engineering practice is to keep the model and the implementation moving together, with the implementation used to **validate** the model. You will see later that much of the difference between OSI and TCP/IP comes down to exactly this point.
text.zh: 第三条值得多想一下。模型是纸上的，纸上讲得通的东西，做出来可能慢，也可能互相打架。所以工程上的好习惯是：模型和实现总是一起走，实现用来**验证**模型。后面你会看到，OSI 和 TCP/IP 的差别，很大程度上就落在这一点上。

chapter.en: OSI: seven layers, one job each

title.en: OSI's seven layers, one sentence each

text.en: **Open Systems Interconnection (OSI)** is a reference model put forward by the International Organization for Standardization (ISO), with **7 layers**. First get to know what each layer does, using your opening of www.unimelb.edu.au as the thread.
text.zh: **开放系统互连** (Open Systems Interconnection, OSI) 是国际标准化组织 (ISO) 提出的参考模型，共 **7 层**。先认识每一层管什么，下面用你打开 www.unimelb.edu.au 这件事做线索。

rows.en: What the application itself has to say
The browser says “give me this web page”
rows.zh: 浏览器说『给我这个网页』

rows.en: How both sides understand the data format: encoding, compression, encryption
rows.zh: 双方对数据格式的理解：编码、压缩、加密

rows.en: Which encoding the text uses, whether to compress
rows.zh: 文字用哪种编码，要不要压缩

rows.en: Managing one conversation: start, end, where to resume after a break
rows.zh: 一次对话的管理：开始、结束、断了从哪里接着来

rows.en: If a download breaks halfway, where to resume
rows.zh: 下载到一半断了，从哪里续传

rows.en: Process to process: delivering to **the right program** on the other machine
rows.zh: 进程到进程：送到对方机器上**对的那个程序**

rows.en: Handing it to the website software on the server, not some other program
rows.zh: 交给服务器上的网站软件，而不是别的程序

rows.en: Machine to machine: crossing one network after another, choosing a route to the target machine
rows.zh: 机器到机器：跨过一个个网络，选路送到目标机器

rows.en: Between two adjacent machines: framing, detecting errors
rows.zh: 相邻两台机器之间：成帧，发现错误

rows.en: The stretch from the laptop to the dorm router
rows.zh: 笔记本到宿舍路由器那一段

rows.en: How bits become signals on the wire
rows.zh: 比特怎样变成线上的信号

rows.en: Wi-Fi radio waves, light in a fibre
rows.zh: Wi-Fi 的无线电波，光纤里的光

text.en: Remember them from the bottom up: **Please Do Not Throw Sausage Pizza Away** (Physical, Data link, Network, Transport, Session, Presentation, Application). The lower the layer, the closer to the wire; the higher, the closer to people. Two pairs are most easily confused: the network layer handles **machine to machine**, while the transport layer handles **process to process**; the data link layer handles **two adjacent** machines, while the network layer handles two machines **separated by many networks**.
text.zh: 从下往上记：**物数网传会表应**。越往下越靠近线，越往上越靠近人。有两对最容易混：网络层管**机器到机器**，传输层管**进程到进程**；数据链路层管**相邻**两台机器，网络层管**隔着很多个网络**的两台机器。

title.en: Keep one thing in mind

body.en: The jobs of the presentation and session layers are not done by separate layers in today's Internet. We will come back here when we reach TCP/IP.
body.zh: 表示层和会话层的活儿，在今天的互联网里并没有单独的层来做。后面讲 TCP/IP 的时候，会回到这里。

title.en: How the seven layers were cut

text.en: Why seven layers, and not five or ten? When OSI cut the layers it followed four principles. Looked at through a specific layer, each one stops being abstract.
text.zh: 为什么是七层，不是五层、十层？OSI 切层的时候，参照了四条原则。每一条，用一个具体的层来看，就不再抽象。

items.en: **Set up a layer only where a different abstraction is needed; each layer's function must be clearly defined.** Example: why are the network layer and the transport layer separate? The network layer's problem is “how to cross a pile of networks to reach that machine”, and a router has to do it at every stop. The transport layer's problem is “once at the machine, which program gets it, and whether to make up for losses”, and only the hosts at the two ends need to care. Different abstractions should be separated; merged, a router would have to worry about things it does not care about at all.
items.zh: **需要不同的抽象，才设一层；每层的功能要定义清楚。** 例：网络层和传输层为什么分开？网络层的问题是『怎么穿过一堆网络到那台机器』，路由器每一站都要做。传输层的问题是『到了机器以后交给哪个程序、丢了要不要补』，只有两端的主机需要管。抽象不同，就该分开；合在一起，路由器就得替它根本不关心的事操心。

items.en: **Draw layer boundaries so that the information flow across the interface is minimal.** Example: all the network layer hands to the link layer is “send this packet to the next hop”; it need not say whether the contents are a web page or an email. The narrower the interface, the less two layers depend on each other, and changing one layer does not drag in another. Conversely, if the link layer had to know what is being carried above it, every new kind of application would require the link layer to change too.
items.zh: **层的边界，要让跨接口的信息流最小。** 例：网络层交给链路层的，只要『这一包发给下一跳』就够了，不必告诉它里面装的是网页还是邮件。接口越窄，两层互相依赖得越少，改一层不牵连另一层。反过来，如果链路层必须知道上面在传什么，那每出现一种新应用，链路层都要跟着改。

items.en: **Have enough layers to keep different functions apart, but few enough that the architecture is not too complex.** Too few: one layer crams in several unrelated functions, and changing one thing affects everything. Too many: each extra layer adds a header to the data and one more handover, making design and debugging harder.
items.zh: **层数要多到能把不同功能分开，又少到架构不至于太复杂。** 太少：一层里塞着好几种不相干的功能，改一处牵全身。太多：每多一层，数据就多一个头、多一次交接，设计和排错都更麻烦。

items.en: **Define each layer's function with reference to internationally standardised protocols.** This way the boundaries drawn between layers let the existing standard protocols each find their place, with nothing to reinvent.
items.zh: **每层的功能，参考国际标准化的协议来定。** 这样各层划出来的边界，正好让已有的标准协议各归其位，不用重新发明。

title.en: What “minimal information flow” means

body.en: It does not mean little data, but little that the two layers need to **negotiate**. A narrow interface means low coupling. Layering works because of this.
body.zh: 不是说数据少，而是两层之间需要**商量的东西**少。接口窄，就是低耦合。分层能成立，靠的就是这一点。

title.en: Putting routing and reliable transfer in one layer
title.zh: 把选路和可靠传输放进一层

prompt.en: When designing a new network, someone proposes putting “routing” and “reliable transfer” in the same layer, since both are about “getting the data there”. Which of OSI's layering principles does this violate?
prompt.zh: 有人设计新网络时提议：把『选路』和『可靠传输』放进同一层，反正都是『把数据送到』。这违反了 OSI 的哪条分层原则？

label.en: A layer is set up only for a different abstraction, and each layer's function must be clearly defined
label.zh: 需要不同抽象才设一层，每层的功能要定义清楚

label.en: There must be few enough layers that the architecture is not too complex
label.zh: 层数要少到不让架构太复杂

feedback.en: Merging actually gives one layer fewer, so this principle is not violated.
feedback.zh: 合并反而少了一层，这条原则并没有被违反。

label.en: Each layer's function must follow internationally standardised protocols
label.zh: 每层的功能要参考国际标准化的协议

feedback.en: This principle is about following standard protocols when dividing, and has nothing to do with “merging two functions”.
feedback.zh: 这条原则说的是参考标准协议来划分，和『合并两种功能』没有关系。

label.en: It violates no principle, and merging even saves a header
label.zh: 没有违反任何原则，合并还省一个头

feedback.en: Saving a header is indeed true; that is the trade-off in the third principle. But routing is something every router must do, while reliable transfer is needed only by the two end hosts; putting different abstractions in one layer makes routers worry about things they do not care about.
feedback.zh: 省一个头确实是真的，这是第三条原则里的权衡。但选路是每个路由器都要做的，可靠传输只有两端主机需要；抽象不同却放在一层，路由器就得替它不关心的事操心。

explain.en: Routing and reliable transfer are two different abstractions: one is “finding a way across a pile of networks”, the other is “making sure nothing is lost or reordered between two programs”. Put together, the function is no longer clearly defined, and routers have to carry a burden they do not need.
explain.zh: 选路和可靠传输是两种不同的抽象：一个是『穿过一堆网络找路』，一个是『保证两个程序之间不丢不乱』。放在一起，功能就不再定义清楚，路由器也要背上它不需要的负担。

title.en: Reading the OSI figure: a router has only the lower three layers
title.zh: 读懂 OSI 图：路由器只有下三层

alt.en: OSI's seven layers: host A and host B each have seven layers, and the two routers each have only the bottom three; the upper four layers' protocols run straight from host to host, while the lower three run hop by hop; the right side lists the unit of data exchanged at each layer
alt.zh: OSI 七层：主机 A 和主机 B 各有七层，两台路由器各只有下面三层；上四层的协议从主机直通主机，下三层的协议一段一段；右侧列出每层交换的数据单位

caption.en: The upper four layers are end to end, the lower three are hop by hop; a router has only the lower three layers
caption.zh: 上四层是端到端，下三层是一段一段；路由器只有下三层

items.en: **Read across**: the protocols of the first four layers (application, presentation, session, transport) run directly from layer k of host A to layer k of host B, **end to end**, and the routers in between take no part. The protocols of the lower three layers (network, data link, physical) run **hop by hop**: host to router, router to router (the internal subnet protocol), router to host.
items.zh: **横着看**：前四层（应用、表示、会话、传输）的协议，是主机 A 的第 k 层直接对主机 B 的第 k 层，**端到端**，中间的路由器不过问。下三层（网络、数据链路、物理）的协议是**一段一段**的：主机到路由器、路由器到路由器（内部子网协议）、路由器到主机。

items.en: **A router implements only the lower three layers**: it only moves the packet towards its destination and need not understand web pages or email. When it receives a frame, it opens only as far as layer 3, reads the destination address, picks the next hop, and sends it on with a new header and trailer.
items.zh: **路由器只实现下三层**：它只管把分组往目标方向送，不需要读懂网页、邮件。收到一个帧，它只拆到第 3 层，读出目标地址，选好下一跳，再换上新的头尾发出去。

items.en: **Communication subnet**: the rounded box in the figure, that is, the network formed by the routers, with a boundary between it and the hosts.
items.zh: **通信子网** (communication subnet)：图里圆角框起来的那一块，也就是路由器们组成的网络，它和主机之间有一条边界。

text.en: What each layer's exchange unit is called
text.zh: 每层交换的数据单位叫什么

text.en: There are many names, but only one rule: **each layer's unit = what the layer above handed down + this layer's header** (the data link layer adds a trailer as well). This matches the encapsulation of lesson 1 exactly: H4 plus data is layer 4's unit, H3 plus a piece is a packet, and what H2 to T2 wrap up is a frame; layer 1 adds no header, so only bits remain. PDU is short for protocol data unit.
text.zh: 名字多，规律只有一条：**每层的单位 = 上一层交下来的东西 + 本层的头**（数据链路层还多加一个尾）。这和第 1 课的封装完全一致：H4 加数据是第 4 层的单位，H3 加一段是分组，H2 到 T2 包起来的是帧；第 1 层不加头，所以只剩比特。PDU 是『协议数据单元』(protocol data unit) 的缩写。

title.en: How far does the router open it

prompt.en: A frame sent by the laptop is forwarded by the dorm router. After receiving it, the router must decide “who to send it to at the next stop”. As far as which layer's header does it need to open it to make this decision?
prompt.zh: 笔记本发出的一个帧，经宿舍路由器转发。路由器收到它之后，要决定『下一站发给谁』。它最多需要拆开到哪一层的头，才能做出这个决定？

label.en: Layer 2: the frame header has the address of the next stop, which is enough
label.zh: 第 2 层：帧头里有下一站的地址，足够了

feedback.en: The layer 2 header only says who to send to on this one link. To route across networks, it has to read the destination machine's address in layer 3.
feedback.zh: 第 2 层的头只说明这一段链路上发给谁。要跨网络选路，得读第 3 层里目标机器的地址。

label.en: Layer 3: read the network layer header, which has the destination machine's address, and pick the next hop from it
label.zh: 第 3 层：读网络层的头，里面有目标机器的地址，据此选下一跳

label.en: Layer 4: it must look at the transport header to know which program to send it to
label.zh: 第 4 层：得看传输层的头才知道发给哪个程序

feedback.en: Which program it goes to is the destination host's business. A router implements only the lower three layers and does not need to look at the transport header.
feedback.zh: 发给哪个程序，是终点主机的事。路由器只实现下三层，不需要看传输层的头。

label.en: Layer 7: it must understand the web request in order to forward it
label.zh: 第 7 层：必须看懂网页请求才能转发

feedback.en: A router does not care about application content; it has no application layer and does not need one.
feedback.zh: 路由器不管应用内容，它既没有应用层，也不需要它。

explain.en: A router implements only the lower three layers: it strips the layer 2 header and trailer, reads the layer 3 destination address, picks the next hop, then sends it on with a new layer 2 header and trailer. The higher layers are left to the hosts at the two ends.
explain.zh: 路由器只实现下三层：剥掉第 2 层的头尾，读第 3 层的目标地址，选好下一跳，再换上新的第 2 层头尾发出去。高层的事，留给两端的主机。

title.en: Origins: from the telephone network to ARPANET

text.en: TCP/IP did not come from nowhere. First look at the world before it appeared. Slides 16 and 17 have only pictures and titles, but each wants to say one thing.
text.zh: TCP/IP 不是凭空来的。先看它出现之前的世界。课件第 16、17 页只有图和标题，其实各自想说一件事。

alt.en: Left: the hierarchical telephone system, with switching offices under a toll office; if one switching office fails, all the users under it are cut off. Right: Baran's distributed mesh network; if a node in the middle fails, data goes around it along the outer ring
alt.zh: 左：层级式的电话系统，交换局挂在长途局下面，一个交换局坏了它下面的用户全部断开；右：Baran 的网状分布式网络，中间一个节点坏了，数据从外圈绕过去

caption.en: A hierarchy breaks easily at a single point; a mesh has several routes to go around
caption.zh: 层级式容易在一点上断开，网状有多条路可以绕

items.en: The **telephone system** is hierarchical: each user connects to a local switching office, which connects to a toll office a level up. It saves wire, but each higher level is a single point: when it fails, the people under it can no longer reach each other.
items.zh: **电话系统**是层级式的：每个用户连到本地的交换局 (switching office)，交换局再连到上一级的长途局 (toll office)。省线，但每个上一级都是单点：它一坏，下面的人互相就联系不上了。

items.en: **Baran's distributed switching system**: nodes are woven into a net, with several paths between any two points. Lose one node and the data goes around it, and the network stays connected. What he wanted was a network that could survive damage.
items.zh: **Baran 提出的分布式交换系统** (distributed switching)：节点织成一张网，任意两点之间有多条路径。坏掉一个节点，数据绕过去，网络依然连着。他想要的就是一个扛得住损坏的网络。

items.en: **ARPANET** was one of the earliest large packet-switched networks, and later grew into the ancestor of the Internet. In December 1969 it had only 4 nodes (UCLA, SRI, UCSB, Utah), and kept adding more institutions; by September 1972 it had more than thirty, with both coasts connected.
items.zh: **ARPANET** 是最早的大型分组交换网络之一，后来长成了互联网的前身。1969 年 12 月只有 4 个节点 (UCLA、SRI、UCSB、Utah)，一路接上更多机构，到 1972 年 9 月已有三十多个，东西两岸都连上了。

text.en: What to remember from these two pages: **a mesh with multiple paths is more resistant to failure than a hierarchy**; ARPANET grew from 4 nodes and was the ancestor of the Internet. The idea of “cut the data into packets and let each find its own way” is covered in more detail in lesson 8, on the network layer.
text.zh: 这两页要记住的是：**网状、多路径的网络，比层级式的更不怕坏**；ARPANET 是从 4 个节点长起来的、互联网的前身。『把数据切成分组，各自找路』这件事，第 8 课讲网络层的时候再细讲。

title.en: How to use this page

body.en: These two slides give only pictures, no text, and are background knowledge. What the exam requires is whatever the slides and the teacher say.
body.zh: 这两页课件只给了图，没有文字，是背景知识。考试怎么要求，以课件和老师的说明为准。

title.en: TCP/IP: made to join different networks together
title.zh: TCP/IP：为了把不同的网络连起来

text.en: After ARPANET grew, a new problem appeared: there is more than one network in the world. Some use telephone lines, some radio, some satellites, each with different rules inside. How can they be joined into a whole?
text.zh: ARPANET 长大以后，出现了一个新问题：世界上不止一张网。有的网用电话线，有的用无线电，有的用卫星，各自内部的规矩都不同。怎样让它们连成一个整体？

text.en: In 1974, Vint Cerf and Bob Kahn gave the answer: **TCP/IP** (Transmission Control Protocol/Internet Protocol). The two later won the 2004 Turing Award.
text.zh: 1974 年，Vint Cerf 和 Bob Kahn 给出了答案：**TCP/IP** (传输控制协议/互联网协议，Transmission Control Protocol/Internet Protocol)。两人后来获得了 2004 年的图灵奖。

text.en: Their method was to add a layer **on top of** the various networks, dedicated to “joining networks to networks”. This layer is called the **Internet layer**: Internet here is just internetwork, meaning “between networks”.
text.zh: 他们的办法，是在各种网络**之上**再加一层，专门负责『把网络和网络连起来』。这一层叫 **Internet 层**（互联网层）：Internet 就是 internetwork，『网络之间』的意思。

title.en: The Internet layer is not the Internet

body.en: The “Internet layer” in the TCP/IP model means the layer that carries packets across networks, and corresponds to OSI's network layer. The “Internet” (the Internet) we talk about is the global network. The names share a source, but one is a layer in a model and the other is an actual network. Do not mix them up.
body.zh: TCP/IP 模型里的『Internet 层』，说的是跨网络送分组的那一层，对应 OSI 的网络层。我们说的『互联网』(the Internet) 是那张全球的网。名字同源，但一个是模型里的一层，一个是实实在在的网络，别混。

text.en: The TCP/IP model has **4 layers** in all, from top to bottom: Application, Transport, Internet and Link. The next page shows which protocols each layer has.
text.zh: TCP/IP 模型一共 **4 层**，从上到下：应用层 (Application)、传输层 (Transport)、互联网层 (Internet)、链路层 (Link)。每一层有哪些协议，下一页看。

text.en: Linking back to lesson 1: TCP provides a **connection-oriented** service and UDP provides a **connectionless** one. If you want reliability, pick TCP; if you want light and quick, pick UDP. Having several protocols in the same layer is exactly so that the layer above has a choice.

prompt.zh: 按 TCP/IP 的四层，下面四个协议依次属于哪一层？DNS、UDP、ICMP、802.11

label.zh: 应用层、传输层、互联网层、链路层

label.en: Application, application, Internet, link
label.zh: 应用层、应用层、互联网层、链路层

feedback.en: UDP and TCP both belong to the transport layer, as two choices within it; UDP is not an application-layer protocol.
feedback.zh: UDP 和 TCP 同属传输层，是传输层的两个选择，不是应用层协议。

label.en: Transport, transport, Internet, link
label.zh: 传输层、传输层、互联网层、链路层

feedback.en: DNS is an application-layer protocol: it is the language applications use to ask and answer about names and addresses, not something that carries data from one program to another.
feedback.zh: DNS 是应用层协议：它是应用之间问答名字和地址的话，而不是把数据从一个程序送到另一个程序。

label.en: Application, transport, link, Internet
label.zh: 应用层、传输层、链路层、互联网层

feedback.en: ICMP is an error-reporting protocol that works with IP and belongs to the Internet layer; 802.11 is Wi-Fi and belongs to the link layer. You swapped these two.
feedback.zh: ICMP 是和 IP 一起工作的报错协议，属于互联网层；802.11 是 Wi-Fi，属于链路层，这两个弄反了。

explain.en: DNS is the application layer, UDP is the transport layer, ICMP is the Internet layer, and 802.11 is the link layer. The way to tell is to ask whom it serves: speaking for applications is the application layer, carrying data between programs is the transport layer, carrying packets across networks between machines is the Internet layer, and carrying frames over one stretch of line is the link layer.
explain.zh: DNS 是应用层，UDP 是传输层，ICMP 是互联网层，802.11 是链路层。判断的办法：看它为谁服务：为应用说话的是应用层，为程序之间送数据的是传输层，为机器跨网络送分组的是互联网层，为一段线路送帧的是链路层。

title.en: Seven layers against four

prompt.en: OSI has 7 layers and TCP/IP only 4. Lining them up, how were the missing 3 layers most likely lost?
prompt.zh: OSI 有 7 层，TCP/IP 只有 4 层。把它们对起来，少掉的 3 层，最可能是怎么少的？

label.en: The presentation and session layers do not stand alone and are folded into the application layer; the data link and physical layers are merged into one
label.zh: 表示层、会话层不单独成层，并进应用层；数据链路层和物理层并成一层

label.en: The transport layer and network layer in the middle were dropped
label.zh: 中间的传输层和网络层被取消了

feedback.en: TCP and IP are exactly the two protocols in the name TCP/IP; these two layers were not dropped, they are its core.
feedback.zh: TCP 和 IP 正是 TCP/IP 这个名字里的两个协议，这两层不但没取消，还是它的核心。

label.en: The application layer at the top and the physical layer at the bottom were dropped
label.zh: 最上面的应用层和最下面的物理层被取消了

feedback.en: The two ends are the least droppable: one end is the application people use, the other is the real wire.
feedback.zh: 两端是最不能取消的：一端是人用的应用，一端是真正的线。

explain.zh: 答案在下一页的对照图里。

caption.en: Slide 9: three layers into one, two layers into one
caption.zh: 课件第 9 页：三层并一层，两层并一层

rows.zh: Vint Cerf 与 Bob Kahn，1974 年

rows.en: Merged into one application layer; the presentation and session layers do not exist in the model
rows.zh: 并成一个应用层；表示层、会话层在模型里不存在

rows.en: The model survived, but the protocols are hardly used
rows.zh: 模型留了下来，协议几乎没人用

rows.en: The protocols succeeded, and today's Internet runs on them
rows.zh: 协议成功，今天的互联网就跑在它上面

text.en: Why does “OSI clearly distinguishes service, interface and protocol” count as an advantage? Lesson 1 explained: a service says what is done, an interface says how to use it, and a protocol says how it is done. With the three kept apart, the model can be laid over any protocol stack, and swapping one layer's protocol does not affect the others. TCP/IP does not distinguish them clearly: its model was drawn from its own protocols, so changing a protocol disturbs more.
text.zh: 『OSI 明确区分服务、接口、协议』为什么算优点？第 1 课讲过：服务说做什么，接口说怎么用，协议说怎么做。三者分开，模型就能套在任何协议栈上，换掉一层的协议，别的层不受影响。TCP/IP 没有明确区分，它的模型是照着自己的协议画出来的，换协议就牵动更多东西。

text.en: TCP/IP's advantage is not in the model but in the **protocols**: IP, TCP and UDP were built and used first, and today's Internet runs on them. The presentation and session layers “not existing” does not mean nobody does their functions, but that this work (encoding, compression, encryption, managing a conversation) is done by the applications themselves.
text.zh: TCP/IP 的优势不在模型，而在**协议**：IP、TCP、UDP 先被做出来、用起来，今天的互联网就跑在它们上面。表示层和会话层『不存在』，不是说它们的功能没人做，而是这些活儿（编码、压缩、加密、管理对话）由应用自己来做了。

chapter.en: Why OSI did not rule the world
chapter.zh: OSI 为什么没统治世界

title.en: Why OSI did not win

prompt.en: OSI was put out by the International Organization for Standardization. The model is tidy, with seven layers divided clearly, yet it did not rule the world, and today's Internet runs TCP/IP. What do you think the main reasons were?
prompt.zh: OSI 由国际标准化组织推出，模型整齐，七层分得清清楚楚，却没有统治世界，今天的互联网跑的是 TCP/IP。你觉得主要原因是什么？

label.en: The idea of layering itself was wrong
label.zh: 分层的想法本身是错的

feedback.en: The idea of layering is exactly right; TCP/IP and this course's five-layer model both use it.
feedback.zh: 分层的想法恰恰是对的，TCP/IP 和本课程的五层模型都在用。

label.en: Things outside the model: complex protocols that were hard to implement, big and slow implementations, and a standard that came at the wrong time
label.zh: 模型之外的东西：协议复杂难实现、实现又大又慢、标准出得不是时候

label.en: ISO was not authoritative enough and nobody listened
label.zh: ISO 不够权威，没人听他们的

feedback.en: Authority was never the problem; ISO is an international standards body. The problem was in the standard itself and when it appeared.
feedback.zh: 权威从来不是问题，ISO 是国际标准组织。问题出在标准本身和它出现的时机。

explain.en: The slides sum it up in three words: bad technology, bad implementations, bad timing. Next we take them one by one.
explain.zh: 课件用三个词概括：bad technology、bad implementations、bad timing。下面一个个展开。

title.en: OSI lost on three counts

text.en: Slide 12 leaves only three words. Behind each word there is a concrete story.
text.zh: 课件第 12 页只留了三个词。每个词后面都有具体的故事。

items.en: **Bad technology**: not all seven layers were reasonable. The session and presentation layers are almost empty, while the network and data link layers are crammed full; both the model and the protocols are complex, and some functions (such as error control and flow control) appear again and again in several layers.
items.zh: **技术差** (bad technology)：七层并不都合理。会话层和表示层几乎是空的，网络层和数据链路层却挤得很满；模型和协议都复杂，有些功能（比如差错控制、流量控制）在好几层里重复出现。

items.en: **Bad implementations**: early OSI implementations were big, clumsy and slow, leaving people with a poor impression. TCP/IP implementations of the same time were free and usable, and as more people used them their faults were fixed one by one.
items.zh: **实现差** (bad implementations)：早期的 OSI 实现又大、又笨、又慢，让人对它没有好印象。同时期的 TCP/IP 实现免费、能用，用的人多了，毛病也被一个个改掉。

items.en: **Bad timing**: look at the figure below.

alt.en: Time on the horizontal axis and activity on the vertical axis: first a peak of research, then a fall to a trough, then a peak of billion-dollar investment; standards land in the trough between the two peaks
alt.zh: 横轴是时间，纵轴是活跃程度：先有一个研究的高峰，再落到谷底，之后升起十亿美元投资的高峰；标准落在两峰之间的谷底

caption.en: Standards land in the trough between the research peak and the investment peak
caption.zh: 标准落在研究和投资两个高峰之间的谷底

text.en: The horizontal axis is time and the vertical axis is “how many people are busy with this”. First comes a wave of research, then a peak as big investment pours in, and **standards** fall, unluckily, in the trough between the two peaks: the excitement of research has faded and big investment has not yet begun, so nobody is paying attention.
text.zh: 横轴是时间，纵轴是『有多少人在忙这件事』。先是研究的热潮，之后是大笔投资涌入的高峰，而**标准**偏偏落在两峰之间的谷底：研究的热度已经退了，大投资还没开始，谁都不上心。

text.en: When OSI's standard came out, TCP/IP had already gained a firm footing in universities and research institutions, while companies were still waiting and watching, none willing to risk money first. The slides ask “when is a good time for a standard?”, and from the figure you can read the answer: too early, and research is not finished, so what is set is half-baked; too late, and everyone has already built their own and nobody wants to change. If the timing is wrong, even the tidiest standard cannot be pushed through.
text.zh: OSI 的标准出来时，TCP/IP 已经在大学和研究机构里站稳了脚跟，而公司们还在观望，谁也不愿先冒险投钱。课件那个问题『什么时候是标准的好时机』，从图里能读出：标准太早，研究还没完，定出来的是半成品；太晚，大家已经各自做了，谁也不愿再改。时机对不上，再整齐的标准也推不开。

title.en: How to read this figure

body.en: This is the usual reading of this figure in textbooks. There is only one point: whether a standard succeeds depends not only on how good it is but on when it appears.
body.zh: 这是教科书里对这张图的常见解读。要点只有一个：标准的成败，不光看它好不好，还要看它出现的时候。

title.en: TCP/IP's four faults

text.en: The winner has faults too. Slide 14 lists four, and for each you can ask: what trouble does this cause?
text.zh: 赢家也有毛病。课件第 14 页列了四条，每一条都能问一句：这会带来什么麻烦？

rows.en: Not a general model; the protocols are **overfitted**
rows.zh: 不是通用模型，协议**过度贴合** (overfitted)

rows.en: The model was drawn from TCP/IP's own protocols and fits only itself
rows.zh: 模型是照着 TCP/IP 自己的协议画出来的，只合它自己的身

rows.en: Using it to describe another protocol stack (such as Bluetooth) does not fit, and it gives little guidance for designing a brand-new network
rows.zh: 拿它去描述别的协议栈（例如蓝牙）就对不上，用来设计全新的网络也没有多少指导

rows.en: Does not distinguish service, interface and protocol
rows.zh: 没有区分服务、接口、协议

rows.en: The three concepts are blurred together
It is hard to say “swap this protocol without touching anything else”, and the dividing lines between layers' jobs are unclear
rows.zh: 不好说清『换掉哪个协议而不动别的』，各层的分工界线不明

rows.en: Does not separate the physical layer from the data link layer
rows.zh: 没有把物理层和数据链路层分开

rows.en: One layer holds two very different jobs
rows.zh: 一个层里装着差别很大的两件事

rows.en: “How signals are sent on the wire” and “how frames are organised and errors found” are taught mixed together and are hard to explain. This course splits them for exactly that reason
rows.zh: 『线上怎样发信号』和『帧怎样组织、出错怎样发现』混着讲，说不清楚。这门课正是因此把它们拆开

rows.en: Minor protocols are deeply entrenched and hard to replace
rows.zh: 次要协议根深蒂固，难以替换

rows.en: Once an old protocol has many users, it cannot be replaced
rows.zh: 老协议用的人多了，就换不掉

rows.en: Any improvement disturbs countless existing devices and software. For example, the move from IPv4 to IPv6 has taken many years (lesson 10)
rows.zh: 想改进，就牵动无数现成的设备和软件。例如从 IPv4 过渡到 IPv6 就走了很多年（第 10 课）

text.en: Compare with the previous page: OSI's strengths are exactly TCP/IP's faults, and the reverse is true too. So the next step is natural: take the best of each.
text.zh: 对照上一页：OSI 的优点，正好是 TCP/IP 的毛病；反过来也成立。所以下一步很自然：取长补短。

title.en: Replying to “OSI is wrong”

prompt.en: A classmate says: “OSI lost to TCP/IP, which shows OSI's layered model is wrong, so let's not study it.” Based on this section, how do you reply?
prompt.zh: 同学说：『OSI 输给了 TCP/IP，说明 OSI 的分层模型是错的，我们别学它了。』根据这一部分的内容，你怎么回应他？

key_points.en: What OSI lost on was its protocols and its timing (complex technology, poor implementations, a standard that came too late), not the idea of layering itself
key_points.zh: OSI 输掉的是它的协议和时机（技术复杂、实现差、标准出得太晚），不是分层的思想本身

key_points.en: OSI's model has value: it clearly separates service, interface and protocol, and is still used to describe and teach networks; this course's five-layer model takes its lower four layers
key_points.zh: OSI 的模型有价值：明确区分服务、接口、协议，今天仍用来描述和讲解网络；本课程的五层模型就取了它的下四层

key_points.en: TCP/IP won because its protocols were built first, were usable and were already widely used, not because its model is better; its model has faults too (not general, does not separate service, interface and protocol, does not separate the physical and data link layers)
key_points.zh: TCP/IP 赢在协议先被做出来、能用、已经被广泛使用，不是因为它的模型更好；它的模型也有毛病（不通用、没分开服务接口协议、没分开物理层和数据链路层）

model_answer.en: You cannot say that. What OSI lost on was its protocols and its timing: the protocols were complex, early implementations were big and slow, and by the time the standard came out TCP/IP was already widely used. None of these is a fault of the idea of layering itself. On the contrary, OSI clearly separates service, interface and protocol, which is a strength of its model, and it is still used to describe and teach networks today; this course's five-layer model takes its lower four layers. TCP/IP won because its protocols were built first and worked well, and its model actually has faults, such as not being general, not separating service, interface and protocol, and not separating the physical layer from the data link layer.
model_answer.zh: 不能这样说。OSI 输掉的是它的协议和时机：协议复杂，早期实现又大又慢，标准出来时 TCP/IP 已经被广泛使用了。这些都不是分层思想本身的错。相反，OSI 把服务、接口、协议明确分开，这是它模型的优点，今天仍用来描述和讲解网络，我们这门课的五层模型就取了它的下四层。TCP/IP 赢在协议先做出来、好用，它的模型反而有毛病，比如不通用、没有分开服务接口协议、没有把物理层和数据链路层分开。

explain.en: A model and a protocol are two different things: the model is the blueprint, and the protocol is what actually runs. Whether a model is good, and whether its companion protocols win, must be judged separately.
explain.zh: 模型和协议是两回事：模型是蓝图，协议是真正跑起来的东西。一个模型好不好，和它配套的协议赢不赢，要分开评价。

title.en: Taking the best of each: this course's five-layer model
title.zh: 取长补短：本课程的五层模型

text.en: Each of the two models has half the merits: OSI's lower half is divided clearly, and TCP/IP's upper half fits reality. This course takes the strengths of both and uses a **5-layer hybrid model**.
text.zh: 两个模型各有一半的好处：OSI 的下半部分分得清楚，TCP/IP 的上半部分合乎实际。本课程取两边的长处，用 **5 层混合模型** (hybrid reference model)。

caption.en: The example on the right: a stack of protocols on each of the browser and the server
caption.zh: 右边的例子：浏览器和服务器各一摞协议

rows.en: TCP/IP's application layer (including the functions of OSI's layers 7, 6 and 5)
rows.zh: TCP/IP 的应用层（含 OSI 的 7、6、5 层的功能）

rows.en: OSI's network layer, that is, TCP/IP's Internet layer
rows.zh: OSI 的网络层，即 TCP/IP 的互联网层

rows.en: The wireless signal of 802.11, light pulses in a fibre
rows.zh: 802.11 的无线信号，光纤里的光脉冲

text.en: Why choose this way? **The lower four layers follow OSI**: the physical layer and the data link layer are two quite different jobs, and only by separating them can they be explained clearly (this is exactly TCP/IP's third fault). **The application layer follows TCP/IP**: in real networks nobody implements OSI's session and presentation layers separately; the work they would do (encoding, compression, encryption, managing a conversation) is done by the application itself or the libraries it uses, and folding it into the application layer fits reality best.
text.zh: 为什么这样取？**下四层用 OSI 的**：物理层和数据链路层是两件很不同的事，分开才讲得清（这正是 TCP/IP 的第三个毛病）。**应用层用 TCP/IP 的**：OSI 的会话层和表示层，在实际的网络里没有人单独实现它们，它们要做的事（编码、压缩、加密、管理一次对话）由应用自己或它用的库来做，并进应用层最合乎实际。

text.en: The 802.11 box takes up two layers in the figure because the Wi-Fi standard specifies both the data link layer (how to share the channel, how to frame) and the physical layer (which wireless signal to use). One standard covering two layers' jobs does not make the two layers one. The same is true of Ethernet.
text.zh: 图里 802.11 一个框占了两层，是因为 Wi-Fi 的标准同时规定了数据链路层（怎样共用信道、怎样成帧）和物理层（用什么无线信号）。一个标准管两层的事，不等于这两层是一层。以太网也是如此。

title.en: From here on

body.en: Every lesson in this course speaks in terms of these five layers. Layer 1, the physical layer, starts with the next lesson.
body.zh: 这门课的每一课，都按这五层说话。第 1 层物理层，从下一课开始。

alt.en: A staircase of five-layer encapsulation: layer 5 has the message M; layer 4 adds H4; layer 3 adds H3 as well; layer 2 adds H2 and a T2 at the end; layer 1 turns it into bits
alt.zh: 五层封装阶梯：第 5 层的消息 M；第 4 层加 H4；第 3 层再加 H3；第 2 层再加 H2 并在后面加 T2；第 1 层变成比特

caption.en: Each layer down wraps one more layer; on the other side it is peeled off layer by layer
caption.zh: 每往下一层，多包一层；到对面，再一层层剥掉

rows.en: Produces the message M, that is, the HTTPS request
rows.zh: 产生消息 M，也就是 HTTPS 请求

rows.en: Adds header H4 (telling the transport layer on the other side which communication this is and which piece)
rows.zh: 加头 H4（告诉对面的传输层：这是哪一次通信、第几块）

rows.en: Adds header H3 (source and destination IP addresses); if too long, it is cut into several pieces, each carrying its own H3
rows.zh: 加头 H3（源和目标 IP 地址）；太长就切成几个，各带一份 H3

rows.en: Adds header H2 and trailer T2 (who to send to on this link; the trailer is used to check for errors)
rows.zh: 加头 H2 和尾 T2（这一段链路上发给谁；尾用来检查错误）
变成无线电波上的比特

text.en: Each layer uses the service of the layer below through the interface (lesson 1), and layers at the same level read and strip each other's headers according to the protocol. Encapsulation adds layer by layer on the way down, and decapsulation on the other side strips layer by layer on the way up.
text.zh: 每一层通过接口使用下一层的服务（第 1 课），同层之间按协议互相读头、剥头。封装一层层往下加，对面解封装一层层往上剥。

text.en: A router on the way opens it only to layer 3: it strips H2 and T2, reads the destination address in H3 to pick the next hop, then puts on a new H2 and T2 leading to the next stretch of line. The source and destination addresses in H3 do not change (lesson 8 covers this in detail). Only at the server end is it opened all the way to M.
text.zh: 路上的路由器只拆到第 3 层：剥掉 H2 和 T2，读 H3 里的目标地址选下一跳，再换上通向下一段线路的新 H2 和 T2。H3 里的源地址和目标地址不变（第 8 课细讲）。服务器那一端，才一路拆到 M。

title.en: Two sets of names

body.en: Unit names often come in two sets: OSI's segment is called TPDU in some textbooks, and it is the same thing. In the exam, follow the slides.
body.zh: 单位的名字常有两套：OSI 的 segment，在有的教材里叫 TPDU，是同一个东西。考试以课件为准。

title.en: What the router changes when forwarding
title.zh: 路由器转发时改了什么

prompt.en: The frame sent by the laptop is forwarded by the dorm router to the next stretch of line on the fibre side. When forwarding, which things in the frame does the router change?
prompt.zh: 笔记本发出的帧，经宿舍路由器转到光纤那一侧的下一段线路。转发时，路由器改变了帧里的哪些东西？

label.en: It puts on a new H2 and T2 leading to the next stretch of line; the source and destination addresses in H3 stay the same, and H4 and M are left untouched
label.zh: 换上通往下一段线路的新 H2 和 T2；H3 里的源、目标地址不变，H4 和 M 原封不动

label.en: It opens the whole frame down to the innermost part, understands the HTTPS request, and repackages it
label.zh: 整个帧拆到最里面，看懂 HTTPS 请求之后重新打包

feedback.en: A router implements only the lower three layers; it does not read anything above layer 4, let alone understand HTTPS.
feedback.zh: 路由器只实现下三层，不会去读第 4 层以上的内容，更不会读懂 HTTPS。

label.en: It changes the destination address in H3 to the next router's address
label.zh: H3 里的目标地址改成下一个路由器的地址

feedback.en: The destination address in H3 is always the final server. “Who is the next stop” is the business of the layer 2 header H2.
feedback.zh: H3 里的目标地址始终是最终要去的服务器。『下一站是谁』，是第 2 层头 H2 的事。

label.en: Nothing changes; the router forwards it unchanged like an extension cord
label.zh: 什么都不变，路由器像一根延长线原样转发

feedback.en: Each link has its own header and trailer, and H2 and T2 have to be replaced with those of the next link.
feedback.zh: 每一段链路各有各的头尾，H2 和 T2 要换成下一段的。

explain.en: H2 and T2 cover only one link, so they are replaced at every hop; H3 covers the end-to-end destination and is carried all the way; H4 and M are matters between the two end hosts, and the router does not touch them.
explain.zh: H2 和 T2 只管一段链路，所以每过一段就换；H3 管的是端到端的目标，一路带着；H4 和 M 是两端主机之间的事，路由器不碰。

title.en: Four things into five layers

prompt.en: Put the following four things into this course's five layers, and give one sentence of reasoning for each: HTTPS; TCP; an IP packet; 802.11 (Wi-Fi).
prompt.zh: 把下面四样东西放进本课程的五层里，并各用一句话说明理由：HTTPS；TCP；一个 IP 分组；802.11 (Wi-Fi)。

key_points.en: HTTPS is at layer 5, the application layer: it is what the browser and the website software say to each other
key_points.zh: HTTPS 在第 5 层应用层：是浏览器和网站软件之间说的话

key_points.en: TCP is at layer 4, the transport layer: it handles process to process, connection-oriented and reliable
key_points.zh: TCP 在第 4 层传输层：管进程到进程，面向连接、可靠

key_points.en: An IP packet is the data unit of layer 3, the network layer: it carries source and destination IP addresses and is responsible for getting across networks to the destination machine
key_points.zh: IP 分组是第 3 层网络层的数据单位：带着源和目标 IP 地址，负责跨网络送到目标机器

key_points.en: 802.11 spans layer 2, the data link layer, and layer 1, the physical layer: it specifies both how the channel is shared and framed, and which wireless signal is used
key_points.zh: 802.11 横跨第 2 层数据链路层和第 1 层物理层：同时规定怎样共用信道、成帧，以及用什么无线信号

model_answer.en: HTTPS is at layer 5, the application layer, and is what the browser and the website software say to each other. TCP is at layer 4, the transport layer; it handles process-to-process communication and is connection-oriented and reliable. An IP packet is the data unit of layer 3, the network layer; it carries the source and destination IP addresses and is responsible for getting across networks to the destination machine. 802.11 is the Wi-Fi standard and spans layer 2, the data link layer, and layer 1, the physical layer: it specifies both how the channel is shared and how frames are formed, and which wireless signal is used.
model_answer.zh: HTTPS 在第 5 层应用层，是浏览器和网站软件之间说的话。TCP 在第 4 层传输层，管进程到进程的通信，是面向连接、可靠的。IP 分组是第 3 层网络层的数据单位，里面带着源和目标 IP 地址，负责跨网络把它送到目标机器。802.11 是 Wi-Fi 的标准，横跨第 2 层数据链路层和第 1 层物理层：它既规定了怎样共用信道、怎样成帧，也规定了用什么无线信号。

explain.en: To tell which layer something is in, ask whom it serves: speaking for applications is layer 5, carrying data between programs is layer 4, carrying packets across networks between machines is layer 3, and carrying frames and signals over one stretch of line is layers 2 and 1.
explain.zh: 判断一个东西在哪一层，就问它在为谁服务：为应用说话是第 5 层，为程序之间送数据是第 4 层，为机器跨网络送分组是第 3 层，为一段线路送帧、送信号是第 2、1 层。
